faqs.a: You must be aged 16 to 47 and attest before your 48th birthday, and you can apply from 15 years and 9 months old. The RAF Reserve Gunner route accepts applicants aged 18 to 54, with a minimum commitment of 27 days per year.
faqs.q: How old do you need to be to join as an RAF Regiment Gunner?

faqs.a: No formal qualifications are required for the RAF Regiment Gunner role, which sets it apart from most RAF trades. During Phase 2 specialist training you will work towards Functional Skills Level 1 qualifications in English and Mathematics. What matters far more is passing the fitness tests, the medical assessment and the Defence Aptitude Assessment, plus meeting nationality and residency rules.
faqs.q: Do I need GCSEs to become a Regiment Gunner?

faqs.a: You must pass the Pre-Joining Fitness Test, including a 2.4 km treadmill run, press-ups and sit-ups, with times set by age and gender. At the Potential Gunner Selection Course you also face a 2 km best-effort run, a 4 kg seated medicine ball throw of 3.1 metres and a 95 kg static deadlift.
faqs.q: What fitness standards must I pass?

faqs.a: You must meet the RAF's nationality and residency criteria, generally UK, Republic of Ireland or Commonwealth citizenship, and you must obtain the security clearance required for the role. Permanent employment is contingent on that vetting, so nationality or connections that prevent clearance can lead to rejection even after passing the other stages of selection.
faqs.q: What nationality do I need for this role?

faqs.a: The minimum commitment is three years after completing Phase 2 specialist training, on top of the training period itself. Many Gunners serve much longer, progressing through the ranks and specialising in fields like sniping, mortars or communications. Leaving before the minimum term is possible only under specific discharge conditions agreed with the service.

headline: Become an RAF Regiment Gunner in 2026
metaDescription: RAF Regiment Gunner recruitment 2026: age 16–47, no formal qualifications needed, PJFT test, Potential Gunner Selection Course and 3-year minimum service.

sections.content:
RAF Regiment Gunners are the ground fighting force of the Royal Air Force, protecting air bases, aircraft and personnel so air and space missions can go ahead. They specialise in combat tactics, weaponry, fieldcraft and force protection, and work in highly trained teams on operations in the UK and overseas.

Day-to-day duties range from patrolling airfields and manning machine guns to detecting and defeating drones, firing anti-tank weapons and acting as pathfinders linking air power to land forces. Gunners can also qualify for parachute or commando courses and serve alongside Special Forces, or join the King's Colour Squadron for ceremonial public duties.
sections.title: What Does an RAF Regiment Gunner Do?

sections.content:
Applicants must be aged 16 to 47 and attest before their 48th birthday; applications can be submitted from age 15 years and 9 months. No formal qualifications are required, and recruits study for Functional Skills Level 1 in English and Mathematics during Phase 2 specialist training. Applicants must meet nationality and residency criteria and pass security vetting, since permanent employment depends on obtaining the right clearance.

Candidates must also pass a medical assessment covering hearing, eyesight and body mass index, plus the Defence Aptitude Assessment. The role carries a minimum commitment of three years after Phase 2 training, and applicants should expect a physically demanding selection process rather than a purely academic one.
sections.title: Entry Requirements at a Glance

sections.content:
Every applicant first takes the Pre-Joining Fitness Test at a local fitness centre, which for Regiment Gunners includes a 2.4 km treadmill run plus press-ups and sit-ups, with pass times varying by age and gender. Men aged 17 to 29 must run 2.4 km in about 13 minutes 20 seconds, while women in the same age group get around 15 minutes 48 seconds.

Successful candidates then attend the Potential Gunner Selection Course at RAF Honington, which includes the RAF Regiment Applicant Selection Test, a 2 km best-effort run after a 500 m warm-up, a seated 4 kg medicine ball throw of 3.1 m and a 95 kg static deadlift. These are minimum standards and candidates are expected to give maximum effort at every event.
sections.title: Fitness Tests: PJFT and PGSC

sections.content:
After selection, recruits complete RAF basic training followed by the Phase 2 Gunner course at RAF Honington, learning weapon handling, fieldcraft, tactics and force protection skills. Training is deliberately arduous, building the fitness, resilience and teamwork the role demands on deployed operations.

Qualified Gunners can progress to lance corporal and beyond, specialise in areas such as sniping, mortars or communications, and earn further qualifications throughout their career. The RAF Reserve also offers a Gunner route for ages 18 to 54 with a commitment of at least 27 days a year, including a two-week residential course.
